guide_enrichment.narrative:
For us, the case for Ohio State creating separation starts with its passing game. Our numbers rate that offense among the nation’s best in pass EPA, while Illinois sits well below average against the pass. We also see continuity behind that advantage: Julian Sayin returned after completing 77 percent of his passes in 2025, and Ohio State brought back eight offensive starters along with 85.8 percent of its offensive-line snaps.

The problem for Illinois extends beyond defending the pass. Our numbers also show a major Ohio State advantage when Illinois runs the ball and when it tries to create scoring opportunities. Still, we are not treating last season’s dominant Ohio State defense as fully interchangeable with this group after eight defensive starters departed. The current matchup indicators remain strongly favorable to Ohio State, but our disagreement with the market is too modest to create enough value at the available price. That is why this remains a pass for us.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are watching Ohio State’s passing offense against the Illinois secondary. Sayin’s accuracy and Jeremiah Smith’s production give Ohio State a direct way to attack the weakest part of the Illinois profile; Smith entered the season with 171 career receptions, 2,709 yards and 29 touchdowns. If Illinois cannot limit efficient completions and prevent Smith from generating chunk gains, we think Ohio State has a clear path to the kind of margin the market is asking it to produce.

recent_game.fact: Ohio State opened the 2026 season with a 56-3 home win over Ball State on Sept. 5.
Jeremiah Smith caught eight passes for 151 yards and two touchdowns against Ball State, with all of that production coming in the first half.
Ohio State had 14 players record a reception against Ball State, its first game with at least 14 receivers since Sept. 22, 2018 against Tulane.
Bo Jackson averaged 9.2 yards per carry in the opener and scored on a career-long 65-yard run.
Ohio State allowed Ball State 165 total yards, including 45 rushing yards and 120 passing yards.
Freshman Legend Bey produced 100 all-purpose yards against Ball State and scored on his first career reception.

quarterback.fact: Julian Sayin is a returning starter and entered 2026 with 15 career starts.

Sayin completed 77.0 percent of his passes in 2025, throwing for 3,610 yards and 32 touchdowns with eight interceptions; his completion percentage led the nation and set Ohio State and Big Ten single-season records.
Sayin entered the Texas game with a 76.4 percent career completion rate and seven career 300-yard passing games.

offensive_personnel.fact: Ohio State returned eight offensive starters for 2026: QB Julian Sayin, RB Bo Jackson, WR Jeremiah Smith, WR Brandon Inniss, OT Phillip Daniels, C Carson Hinzman, OG Luke Montgomery and OG Austin Siereveld.
Ohio State lost three offensive starters from 2025: guard Tegra Tshabola and tight ends Max Klare and Will Kacmarek.
Ohio State returned 85.8 percent of its offensive-line snaps among players who logged at least 100 snaps in 2025, the highest listed continuity rate among Power Four teams.
After the opener, Ohio State's starting offensive line had combined for 146 games played and 93 starts.
The experienced offensive linemen listed in the guide included Carson Hinzman with 36 career starts, Austin Siereveld with 21, Phillip Daniels with 17 and Luke Montgomery with 17.
Wide receivers Devin McCuin, Kyle Parker and Brandon Inniss entered the Texas week with 28, seven and seven career starts, respectively; McCuin transferred from UTSA and Parker transferred from LSU.
Tight end Hunter Welcing transferred from Northwestern with 11 career starts, while Mason Williams transferred from Ohio with 26 career starts.
Bo Jackson led Ohio State with 1,090 rushing yards on 179 carries in 2025 and recorded six 100-yard games in his first 12 outings.

defensive_personnel.fact: Ohio State returned three defensive starters for 2026: cornerback Jermaine Mathews Jr., defensive end Kenyatta Jackson Jr. and safety Jaylen McClain.

Ohio State lost eight defensive starters from 2025: defensive tackles Tywone Malone Jr. and Kayden McDonald, defensive end Caden Curry, linebackers Arvell Reese and Sonny Styles, safeties Caleb Downs and Lorenzo Styles, and cornerback Devin Igbinosun.

Ohio State added experienced defensive transfers James Smith and Qua Russaw from Alabama, John Walker from UCF, Christian Alliegro from Wisconsin, Earl Little Jr. from Florida State and Beau Atkinson from North Carolina.
Safety Earl Little Jr. transferred from Florida State after leading the Seminoles with 76 tackles in 2025 and earning All-ACC recognition.
Linebacker Christian Alliegro entered 2026 with 127 career tackles and eight sacks after transferring from Wisconsin.
Defensive end Kenyatta Jackson Jr. recorded 11 tackles for loss and 6.5 sacks in 2025.

coaching_changes.fact: Ohio State's listed 2026 coordinators are defensive coordinator Matt Patricia, offensive coordinator Arthur Smith and special teams coordinator Robby Discher.
Tyler Bowen is the run game coordinator and offensive line coach, while Billy Fessler is the pass game coordinator and quarterbacks coach.

offensive_context.fact: Through the opener, Ohio State averaged 56 points, 434 passing yards and 237 rushing yards per game.
Ohio State converted 45.5 percent of its third downs and scored on every red-zone possession in the opener.
Jeremiah Smith entered the Texas week with 171 career receptions, 2,709 receiving yards and 29 receiving touchdowns.

defensive_context.fact: Ohio State ranked first nationally in 2025 in scoring defense at 9.3 points allowed per game, total defense at 219.1 yards per game and passing defense at 129.7 yards per game.
Since the start of the 2024 season, Ohio State had allowed 37 touchdowns in 31 games and had held nine opponents without a touchdown.
Ohio State allowed opponents to convert 21.4 percent of third downs in the 2026 opener.

special_teams.fact: Punter Joe McGuire returned as a starter, while kicker Jayden Fielding and long snapper John Ferlmann were listed among the departed starters.

other_relevant.fact: Ohio State's schedule lists Illinois as a home opponent on Sept. 26, 2026.
Ohio State played 21 true freshmen in its season-opening win over Ball State.
